sources.entry: WikiDocs - A databaseless markdown flat-file wiki engine. (Source Code) MIT PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Wiki|Docs is a databaseless, markdown flat-file wiki engine that stores pages as portable Markdown files, offered as a desktop app or a self-hosted Docker service.
summary.what_it_does: Wiki|Docs 2 is a TypeScript rewrite with a NestJS backend, Angular web client, and Electron desktop app. It stores wiki content as plain Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, with no database required. A standalone desktop app keeps the wiki on the local machine. A Docker image can host the same data remotely, and the desktop app can sync with that remote instance. The editor is described as WYSIWYG and supports KaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, syntax highlighting, and image uploads including from the clipboard. Pages can be grouped into namespaces, browsed publicly or privately, and revised without limit. The README also describes REST APIs with Swagger documentation at /api/.
use_cases: Offline desktop note-taking with sync to a server
Wiki content for use with LLM tools
how_to_run: Or use docker-compose.yml with image zavy86/wikidocs:2, environment MODE (public|private) and SECRET, volume datasets:/var/lib/wikidocs/datasets, port 3210:3210
Desktop: download the latest desktop release and run the installer
notable: Plain Markdown flat files with no database, so content stays portable
Standalone Electron desktop app plus optional self-hosted Docker instance
Desktop-to-remote sync configured from the desktop app's Settings menu
Version 2 is a full TypeScript rewrite; the original PHP version lives on a separate branch
caveats: Migrating from version 1.x requires a full backup and a manual move of the homepage document to the root directory
Docker setup uses port 3210 instead of the legacy port 80 and a new dataset path
Sync requires hosting the application yourself to reach a remote instance
